title.narrative: Food security&resilient livelihoods, focus on earthquake affected families through civil society strengthening - SUSTAIN

description.narrative: Overall Objective: Contribution to improved livelihoods in local food systems for resilient communities in Jajarkot and Rukum West Districts. Project Objectives/ Outcomes: 1,750 earthquake affected households in Jajarkot and Rukum West have improved their food and nutrition security, and the civil society and local governments promote climate resilient and nutrition-sensitive agriculture and economic resilience programsIndicators: The targeted households (1,750) have at least 10 months of food sufficiency in their house by the end of the project. (MAHFP)70% (210 out of 300) of trained women and youth households increase their annual cash income by 20% by the end of the projectClimate resilience is anchored in the local development plans and the share in the budget is at least 5% by the end of the project

Target group and intervention area: 2,500 marginalized HHs (earthquake affected, Dalits, Janajatis, women, youth, PWD) in 2 municipalities in Jajarkot, Rukum West districtsIndirect Target Groups: The project’s indirect beneficiaries include the entire population of Barekot Municipality and Aathabiskot Rural Municipality, totaling 57,922 individuals (35,917 in Aathabiskot and in Barekot 22,005). They will benefit indirectly from government policies and community-focused awareness campaigns on topics such as community seed banks, LANN+ and SIFS sessions and irrigation projects. Additionally, private sector actors, cooperatives, and local and provincial governments will gain from the policy formulation activities facilitated by the project, fostering an enabling environment for sustainable development and climate resilience.

The project, implemented by RRN, MIC, and FTG, strengthens food security, income, and disaster resilience in earthquake-affected areas of Jajarkot and Rukum West. Through community consultations and coordination with government and civil society, it promotes climate-adapted agriculture, nutrition-sensitive interventions, and inclusive capacity building. It supports 1,750 households prioritizing women, marginalized groups, smallholder farmers, youth, and PWDs—and provides entrepreneurship and technical skills to 300 selected youth and women. Engagement with 22 CBOs and local governments across 14 wards fosters capacity building, policy advocacy, and climate-smart agriculture with community participation.
